conflicts.description: e-Shram upper age limit: Objectives page (updated 11-Sep-2026) says age 16 years or above with no upper cap. FAQ Q11 on beta.eshram.gov.in says 16-59 years. PIB PRID 2303053 says 16 years and above. Social Security (Central) Rules 2026 Rule 48 requires completed sixteen years of age with no upper cap for unorganised/gig registration under s.113; Rule 49(4) ceases gig scheme eligibility at age sixty.
conflicts.recommended_primary_source: Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026 Rule 48 for Code registration; for the e-Shram portal operational FAQ, disclose both statements and do not invent a cap.

conflicts.description: MoLE explainer attributes wage-period fixation and payment timelines to Section 6 of Code on Wages. Code on Wages (Central) Rules 2026 Rule 3 cites section 6(5) for calculating minimum rate of wages, not wage periods. Explainer section numbering is TIER 3 and must not be treated as India Code text.
conflicts.recommended_primary_source: Code on Wages (Central) Rules, 2026 and India Code Act text (bitstream not downloaded this session).

conflicts.description: Four Codes commenced 21 Nov 2025. CLC still points workers to SAMADHAN. Prior verified SAMADHAN homepage/FAQ listed Payment of Wages Act 1936, Minimum Wages Act 1948, Industrial Disputes Act 1947. MoLE list-of-enactments page dated 2026-01-10 still listed repealed pre-Code Acts. PIB said SAMADHAN under revamp. This session SAMADHAN returned HTTP 503.
conflicts.recommended_primary_source: Gazette commencement notifications + Central Rules 2026 for the law; SAMADHAN/CLC as the filing channel only, not as the statement of applicable Act names.

conflicts.description: NALSA FAQ first answer states Supreme Court income ceiling as less than rupees twelve thousand or higher amount prescribed by Central Government. Same FAQ later table/paragraph and legal-aid page state less than Rs 5 lakh for Supreme Court.
conflicts.recommended_primary_source: https://nalsa.gov.in/legal-aid/ (Rs 5 Lakh) plus Legal Services Authorities Act 1987 canonical text (not downloaded this session).

conflicts.description: e-Shram FAQ Q24 text as extracted: 'What if after registration on e-Shram the unorganised worker moves to organised sector?' Answer: 'In case if a worker moves to unorganised sector, he/she will only be entitled for benefits defined for organised sector workers.' Question and answer refer to opposite sectors. Do not use this Q&A without human review.
conflicts.recommended_primary_source: Do not ingest this Q&A as a right.

conflicts.description: PIB 9 Dec 2025 states aggregators 'are now required to contribute 1-2% of annual turnover capped at 5% of payments'. Additional FAQs 16.03.2026 Q15 says the contribution 'will be notified by the Central Government'. Rules 2026 provide Form-XX assessment using the % notified under s.114(4). The specific percentage in force is therefore PENDING/UNCONFIRMED as a Gazette-notified number.
conflicts.recommended_primary_source: Additional FAQs Q15 + Rule 49 until a Gazette rate notification is located.
